messages:
milan: Repro in our Go sampleapp: generator stream goroutine hangs when canceling from inside the Recv loop. Seen on Linux CI and local.

milan: Minimal snippet pasted below — simple consumer cancels ctx when it sees <END> and then process sometimes never exits.

```
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
g := client.Generator(ctx, &pb.GenRequest{Prompt: "...", MaxTokens: 512})
for {
  tok, err := g.Recv()
  if err != nil {
    log.Printf("recv err: %v", err)
    break
  }
  fmt.Print(tok.Text)
  if strings.Contains(tok.Text, "<END>") {
    cancel() // cancel from inside consumer
  }
}
```

milan: After cancel the app sometimes stays alive; pprof shows a goroutine stuck in a channel send in the internal generator run() path.

devon: That pattern should be supported but only if the producer respects ctx. Our internal generator has a couple of send sites that do plain `out <- chunk` without checking ctx.Done(), so sender can block forever if consumer stops reading.

sasha: can you paste the goroutine dump? we want to confirm `chan send` and the source lines. If it's the plain send then select+ctx.Done() will fix it.

milan: dump from CI attached (shortened):

```
goroutine 12 [chan send]:
	github.com/redwood/runtime/gen.(*generator).run(0xc0000a4000)
	/internal/runtime/gen/stream.go:198 +0x94
	created by github.com/redwood/runtime/gen.(*generator).start
	/internal/runtime/gen/stream.go:145 +0x66

goroutine 1 [running]:
	main.main()
	/sampleapps/gen-repro/main.go:52 +0x10f
```

tara: yep that's the send site. Quick fix: always do `select { case out <- v: case <-ctx.Done(): return }` when sending, and make Recv() return context.Canceled if ctx is done. Also add a Stop/Close helper on the Generator type so callers can call g.Stop() from consumer code instead of cancelling an ambient ctx.

devon: Agreed. We'll add a `sendOrCancel(ctx, out, v)` helper and update the two offending sites. Add unit test where consumer cancels from inside Recv loop and assert no goroutines leaked.

milan: question: behavior change — Recv used to return io.EOF on stream end. On active cancel should we return context.Canceled? Callers might not check for it.

sasha: semantically returning context.Canceled on active cancellation is correct. We'll document it in CHANGELOG and call out in the SDK migration notes. Add `errors.Is(err, context.Canceled)` example in docs.

devon: I'll draft the PR on branch fix/gen-cancel and include the repro test, helper, and a short sampleapp change recommending `defer g.Stop()` usage.

sasha: opened draft PR https://github.com/redwood/sampleapps/pull/1481 with failing test and repro. Assigned to devon.

ci-bot: build queued for branch fix/gen-cancel (tests: unit,integration) — ETA ~5m.

milan: timeline? would prefer before the next 0.9.x patch.

devon: targeting EOD tomorrow; if green will merge and backport to release/0.9.

milan: thanks — ping here when merged. :thumbsup:
